calc_defs.rationale: SysML, paper Eq.1 and Python agree: kills inside ZIDA / total incursions.
SysML matches paper Eq.2 (denom rM); Python uses rB, which respects the Table 20 [0,1] bound that Eq.2 violates. Python accepted; paper errata candidate.

Spec 025 (Article VI section-9) reconciled _compute_moe1 with Eq.5: the '1 -' complement and the evasion penalty (1+E/N) were restored, so the outer aggregation 1 - Sum(tef)/(N*Tmax) now matches the calc def. Inner per-engagement tef/penalty/t_ev and the per-aircraft T_PEA (Spec 018) are below calc-def granularity (sanctioned, like MOE-2/MOE-3). Closes the SR-4b ESCALATE backlog.
Outer aggregation (Eq.10, Sum/N) matches. Inner per-step P_track was upgraded to angular acuity (Spec 016), below calc-def granularity — sanctioned, not a drift.
Outer aggregation (Eq.19, Sum/N) matches. Inner term is the multi-shot cumulative P_neut over continuous firing distances (Spec 015/017), below calc-def granularity.

SysML (min+max)/2 is the update INTERVAL = the paper's MOP-1 ([1,60] s). Python's _compute_mop1 is an emergent heading-update COUNT — a different quantity. Re-bind the calc def to the update_interval_s config parameter; no formula change (metric-neutral).
SysML, paper (Table 18) and Python agree: the maximum acquisition distance.
SysML reports the envelope WIDTH (max-min), Python the MAX, the paper Table 20 the interval [0.5,14]. A reported constant that feeds no computation - representation choice.
